questions.question: A shipping paper:

options.text: Is not needed for most hazardous material shipments.
Is required for all hazardous material shipments.
Can be kept in a digital file.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is required for all hazardous material shipments.
questions.explanation: Shippers must provide shipping papers for all hazardous materials. These papers inform others about the risks of the materials.

questions.question: Exhaust system parts should:
questions.explanation: Exhaust system parts must not leak or be broken. Leaks allow poisonous fumes to enter the cab or sleeper berth.

questions.question: When speeding up on a slippery surface like a wet road, a driver should:

options.text: Not worry about the road surface.

questions.explanation: Always accelerate slowly when road conditions are slippery.

questions.question: How often must hazardous materials employees be trained and tested?
questions.explanation: All drivers must be trained on the security risks of transporting hazardous materials and how to respond to threats. Training and testing must happen at least once every three years.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Front tire tread of 3/32 of an inch

questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check that tires have enough tread. Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. Tire sizes must match.

questions.question: Rims with welding repairs:

options.text: Are acceptable when traveling under 40 mph.

questions.explanation: Wheels or rims that have been welded should never be used.

questions.question: When checking tires, which finding is not a problem?

options.text: Front tire tread of at least 4/32 of an inch
Using radial and bias-ply tires together

questions.correctAnswerText: Front tire tread of at least 4/32 of an inch
questions.explanation: When checking tires, make sure air pressure is not too low or too high. Front tires must have at least 4/32 inch of tread. Do not mix radial and bias-ply tires.

questions.question: In very hot weather, tires should be checked often because:

options.text: Air pressure may increase as the temperature rises.
The tread wears faster in hot weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air pressure may increase as the temperature rises.
questions.explanation: Air pressure increases with temperature. Pay close attention to tire mounting and pressure in hot weather.

questions.question: If a load is on one side of a trailer, the trailer may:

options.text: Lean to one side during turns.
Be easier to steer during turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean to one side during turns.
questions.explanation: Loading weight on one side of a trailer causes it to lean to that side. This increases the risk of rollover during turns and lane changes.

questions.question: Baffled tanks:

options.text: Are damaged and should not be used.
Reduce liquid surge while allowing liquid to flow through the tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce liquid surge while allowing liquid to flow through the tank.
questions.explanation: Baffled tanks have holes that let liquid flow through. This prevents front-to-back surge but does not stop side-to-side surge.

questions.question: A tank truck usually has:
questions.explanation: Tank trucks usually have high centers of gravity. This makes them harder to control. Be careful about cargo movement when transporting liquids.

questions.question: You can avoid distracted driving by:
questions.explanation: Distractions while driving can be physical or mental. To avoid distraction: pre-program radio stations, plan your route ahead, avoid difficult conversations, adjust mirrors before driving, and do not eat, drink, or smoke while driving.

questions.question: When stopping, you should apply the brake pedal by:
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down slowly and smoothly. Gradual braking keeps your vehicle under control.

questions.question: If you notice a safety or mechanical problem with your vehicle while driving, you should:

options.text: Stay quiet and see if the problem goes away.
Write a report that describes your concerns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Write a report that describes your concerns.
questions.explanation: At the end of each day, write a report about any vehicle problems. Note any issues that could affect safety or cause mechanical breakdown.

questions.question: When crossing traffic with a combination vehicle, you should:

options.text: Assume other drivers will make room for your vehicle.
Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to safely cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to safely cross.
questions.explanation: Combination vehicles need more space than other vehicles. Always wait for a large enough gap in traffic before entering or crossing.

questions.question: Rough acceleration is:
questions.explanation: Always accelerate smoothly and gradually. Jerky acceleration can damage your vehicle.

questions.question: If corrosive materials leak in a trailer, the trailer should be:

options.text: Left to air dry without washing.

questions.explanation: Always wash parts exposed to corrosive liquids thoroughly with water.

questions.question: To make your vehicle more visible during the day, you should use:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights for best visibility, even during the day. High beam headlights can be dangerous around other drivers.

questions.question: Before loading or unloading flammable liquids, the engine should be:
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before loading or unloading flammable liquids. Only leave it running if you need it to operate a pump.

questions.question: If you must stop quickly while transporting liquids, you should use the:
questions.explanation: Use the stab braking method for quick stops with liquid cargo. Be careful when steering and braking together, as your vehicle may tip over, especially if it has a high center of gravity.
